net.lemnik.eodsql.spi

Class Context<A extends Annotation>

  • java.lang.Object
    • net.lemnik.eodsql.spi.Context<A>
  • Type Parameters:
    A - the annotation type decorating the method that is being invoked

    public class Context<A extends Annotation>
extends Object

    Stores the Context information of a single method call. This type is used to store objects such as the Connection, the Statement or ResultSet. Each object stored is wrapped in a Resource object. The Context object also stores the Method being invoked and the parameters it has been invoked with.

    By default when a method call is completed, the Context is closed causing all of the resources it holds to be closed and released as well. Sometimes however this is undesired behaviour (for example with a DataIterator), and the setAutoclose(boolean) method can be invoked to change this.

    The Context object also stores the return-value that will be returned from the invoked method. This value may be changed any number of times during a single method call.

    Author:
    Jason Morris

    • Constructor Detail

      • Context

        public Context(A annotation,
               Object[] parameters)

        Create a new Context object with a specified annotation and an array of parameters. The annotation specified should be the one that caused this Context to be created. The Context should only live for the duration of a single Method invocation.

        The Context class elegantly accepts null parameter arrays, turning them into empty arrays here. Specifying null as the annotation is also legal, but may result in undefined behaviour. The default method implementations have no need of the annotation during their execution however.

        Parameters:
        annotation - the annotation containing the methods invocation details
        parameters - the parameters passed to the method being invoked

      • Context

        public Context(Context<A> parentContext,
               Object[] newParameters)
        throws IllegalStateException,
               NullPointerException
        Creates a new Context object based on a given "parent" Context with new parameters. This constructor will copy the annotation and all of the current resources from the parentContext into itself. Resources added to the parent context after this construction will not affect the new Context.

        This context is read-only. Calling setResource(Resource) will throw an IllegalStateException. Calling close() on this context is a no-op, i.e. no resources will be freed when calling this. It is the responsibility of the parent context to free the resources.

        Parameters:
        parentContext - the context to copy the state from
        newParameters - the new parameters
        Throws:
        IllegalStateException - if the parent Context is already closed
        NullPointerException - if the parent Context is null

      • getReturnValue

        public Object getReturnValue()
        Returns the current value that is expected to be returned from this Context. Sine a Context represents the internals of a method invocation, this value represents what will be returned from that invocation. The value may optionally change any number of times during the method invocation, and may at any time be null.
        Returns:
        the current value that will be returned when this Context is closed

      • setReturnValue

        public void setReturnValue(Object returnValue)

      • setResource

        public void setResource(Resource<?> resource)

        Sets a resource in this Context. To avoid naming problems, resources are mapped based on their types. A Context cannot hold more than one Resource of a given type. If a Resource of the specified type already exists in this Context, it will be overwritten by the one specified here.

        Invoking this method with a null Resource object will result in a NullPointerException.

        Parameters:
        resource - the Resource to place into this Context

      • getResource

        public <T> Resource<T> getResource(Class<T> resourceType)
                            throws IllegalStateException
        Return a specified Resource object based on it's type. Requesting a Resource that does has not been set will return null, while requesting a Resource that has been closed will thrown an IllegalStateException.
        Type Parameters:
        T - the type of Resource to fetch from this Context
        Parameters:
        resourceType - the Class descriptor of the Resource type to fetch
        Returns:
        the Resource of the specified type that was stored in this Context, or null if none of the requested type was stored
        Throws:
        IllegalStateException - if either this Context or the requested Resource is closed

      • setAutoclose

        public void setAutoclose(boolean autoclose)
        Sets whether or not to automatically close this Context when it returns. If the value returned will still need to hold resources in this Context (for example a connected DataSet), this should be set to false. By default a Context is in auto-close mode when it is created.
        Parameters:
        autoclose - false to stop the Context from being closed when it's method returns

      • isAutoclose

        public boolean isAutoclose()

      • close

        public void close()
           throws SQLException
        Explicitly close this Context. This method needs to be invoked to close any remaining Resources that this Context still holds if the Context is not in auto-close mode. This method is a no-op if the Context is already closed.
        Throws:
        SQLException - if one of the Resources cannot be closed
        See Also:
        setAutoclose(boolean), getResource(java.lang.Class)
